mechanism.old: At 51e820c1d, the multi-changed-ID branch replays changedIds for every selected label and calls nextSource with per-ID binary occurrence searches. The one-ID branch already streamed. This is repeated replay and point search, not a claim that each old nextSource rescanned every occurrence.
mechanism.new: changedIds is consumed once. Each sourcesForId cursor walks call ordinals once and merges its reconstruction target. Up to 64 live label cursors use a deduplicating heap. A 65th nonempty cursor switches to scalar streaming through sortedLabels; neither changed IDs nor all holders are materialized in production.
mechanism.cascade: A single pending identity displaces 129 historical IDs in the injected same-candidate fixture. This exceeds the cursor cap without making a history-sized heap or ID map. Exact occurrence count is 258, with old salt i and new salt i+1 for every historical ID.
mechanism.ordering: The persistent fallback encodes labels as unsigned big-endian 64-bit prefixes in 16-byte keys, uses identity hashing and an existing IdFactBatch/IdTrieReader, and emits distinct keys in trie order. Heap and trie paths both deduplicate shared holder labels.
mechanism.complexityLimit: This removes per-holder repair replay. It does not establish linear total collision resolution: the deliberate same-candidate salt adversary still requires candidate retries, reflected in the 17548 fact lookups. No suffix-replay fallback or legitimate-input unsupported guard was introduced.

stateAndCapacity.cursors: At most 64 heap entries plus the admitted 65th source generator; the readers set is fixed at at most 65. All use the snapshot fact reader, not a separate ROW reader/cache per historical ID.
stateAndCapacity.tail: For P seed identities, each repair removes one frontier before inserting at most one displaced owner. Terminal IDs grow only when a frontier ends. Frontier/terminal count is at most P, not historical cascade length; seed and identifier byte sizes remain input-dependent.
stateAndCapacity.scalarSpill: Each empty-valued key charges 16+480=496 bytes. The >65536 threshold flushes after at most 133 entries (65968 charged bytes), not a claimed 128-entry buffer. Sorting also holds a fixed chunk-sized array. The batch readback and final trie reader each have 64 KiB charged node caches; the group appender has its existing 256 KiB buffer. These individual caps are not a whole-heap measurement.
stateAndCapacity.triePath: 128-bit keys and four-bit levels bound a traversal path to 32 levels; leaves hold at most eight entries.
stateAndCapacity.disk: Fallback writes one committed group through the existing persistent descriptor. Scratch trie roots are unreachable from published history; durableEnd increases while published roots and aggregate/liveBytes remain unchanged. Written and superseded nodes are journal garbage, subject to existing pinned compaction, not zero storage. At 129 cascaded IDs the measured extra durable bytes are 9120; at two IDs they are zero. No aggregate or 100000-call capacity acceptance is inferred.
stateAndCapacity.rowWindow: Existing shared ROW reader retains 32768 bytes with a 49152-byte replacement transient in the measured warm fixture. Decoded-holder WeakRef coverage is separate from complete retained heap; no history-sized array is permitted in production.
stateAndCapacity.finally: Merge finally returns admitted readers and changed iterator; sorter finally releases its pinned descriptor. New sorter tests preserve original input-error identity and close after early consumer stop. Existing #3919 suites pass 11/29 and 3/20, without assertion or production changes.
